title: Connecting Al-Muddaththir: the whole surah: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
source: Written for quran/y9 lesson 22 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Connecting Al-Muddaththir rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 22. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

timeline.text: Arise and warn; the Day is hard for the disbelievers
The arrogant man; Saqar and its keepers
Oaths; each soul held by its deeds; the four answers
Why do they turn away? It is a reminder

panels.title: Scenes help hifdh
points: Know which scene you are in

keywords.def: revision of what is already memorised

questions.q: In the portal response box, write one sentence per scene (sentence starter: 'The surah opens with ...').
Which scene has the four answers?
Chain recitation: the class recites the whole surah one scene each, in rota order; then complete your summary. Today's rota group recites 74:38 to 56 to the teacher.
questions.a: Whole surah recited across the class; summary complete.

questions.q: Extend: pick the ayah that moves you most and explain why.
questions.a: Personal response with a correct reference.

questions.q: Stretch: recite the whole surah alone.
questions.a: All 56 ayat with no more than four prompts.

options: people turning away from the reminder
questions.a: A) people turning away from the reminder. The last scene: they flee like frightened donkeys; it is a reminder for whoever wills.

questions.q: The surah ends: 'He is worthy of taqwa and worthy of ...'
Think again: If the surah were a story in four scenes, what would the scenes be?
questions.a: The call to rise and warn (1 to 10); the arrogant denier (11 to 31); the oaths and each soul's pledge (32 to 48); the turning away and the reminder (49 to 56).
